question: Who among the following was the third Vice-President of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**V V Giri.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Varahagiri Venkata Giri** 10 August 1894 — 24 June 1980 **was an Indian politician and activist from Berhampur in Odisha.
 
• Giri was honoured by the Government of India with the Bharat Ratna in 1975. Giri died **on 24 June 1980.**
 
• Giri was elected the third vice president of India on **13 May 1967,** a post he held for nearly two years till** 3 May 1969.**
 
• Giri was the first vice president to not complete his full term in office on account of being elevated to the office of the president and was the third vice president to be elected to the presidency.
 
• The 4th President of India from** 24 August 1969 to 24 August 1974** and 3rd vice president of India from **13 May 1967 to 3 May 1969.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **John Adams,** a remarkable political philosopher, served as the second President of the United States (1797-1801), after serving as the first Vice President under President George Washington.
 
• There have been** 49 vice presidents **of the United States since the office came into existence** in 1789.**
 
• Husain, Jamia became closely associated with the Indian freedom movement. He was awarded the Bharat Ratna (India's highest civilian honour)** in 1963.**
 
• He believed in the total development of children can take place through Basic Education, which is craft centred, creative, productive, and self-supporting. According to him, productive work is an instrument of education.
 
• Bharat is My Home is an excerpt from the speech of President** Dr. Zakir Hussain.** He delivered this speech** in 1967, **after taking oath as President. He had also been the Governor of Bihar before becoming President.
 
• Gopal Swarup Pathak** (26 February 1896 – 4 October 1982)** was the fourth vice president of India from **August 1969 to August 1974.** He was the first Indian vice president not to succeed his superior as President.
